original_question: Let [Gamma] be a point on the smoothable component of Hilb_d(A^3) whose tangent space has dimension 3d+6. Is the singularity of Hilb_d(A^3) at [Gamma] smoothly equivalent to the cone point over the Grassmannian Gr(2,6)?
target_in_paper: Problem XXVII ("Mildly singular points of Hilb^d(A^3)") in §2.6, together with the definitions of the smoothable component (§2.1) and smooth equivalence (§2.6).
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact open problem very closely: it has the right ambient moduli space (the smoothable component of Hilb^d(A^3)), the right tangent-space condition (dimension 3d+6), and the right proposed local model (the cone point over Gr(2,6)). It also correctly asks about smooth equivalence of singularities rather than isomorphism of schemes.
missing_details: The paper works over an algebraically closed field k, so the ambient space should be written as A^3_k and the Hilbert scheme as Hilb^d(A^3_k) or Hilb_d(A^3_k) (§1.3).
The question should quantify d and the point [Γ]: namely, for every integer d >= 1 and every closed point [Γ] with the stated property (§2.6).
The smoothable component should be defined explicitly as the closure of the locus of length-d smooth subschemes of A^3_k, equivalently the closure of the locus of d distinct reduced k-points (§2.1).
The tangent-space hypothesis should be stated as dim_k T_[Γ] Hilb^d(A^3_k) = 3d+6, where T_[Γ] denotes the Zariski tangent space (§2.6 context).
The phrase "the singularity at [Γ]" should be made precise as the completed local singularity of Hilb^d(A^3_k) at the closed point [Γ] (§2.6).

The phrase "smoothly equivalent" should be defined: the paper means equivalence after adjoining formal power-series variables to the completed local rings; it also gives an equivalent geometric reformulation via a common smooth cover (§2.6).
The comparison singularity should identify the relevant point as the vertex (cone point) of the affine cone over Gr(2,6), conventionally in its Plücker embedding (§2.6, Problem XXVII).

No extra hypotheses about characteristic zero, homogeneity, polynomial degree, nilpotency, or phrases such as "for all sufficiently large m" belong to this problem; adding them would go beyond the paper.
refined_question: Let k be an algebraically closed field. For every integer d >= 1 and every closed point [Γ] in the smoothable component of Hilb^d(A^3_k) (that is, in the closure of the locus of d distinct reduced k-points), assume that dim_k T_[Γ] Hilb^d(A^3_k) = 3d+6. Must the completed local singularity of Hilb^d(A^3_k) at [Γ] be smoothly equivalent, in the sense of §2.6, to the vertex of the affine cone over the Grassmannian Gr(2,6) in its Plücker embedding?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, if C denotes the affine cone over Gr(2,6) and v its vertex, is it true that for every such [Γ] there exists a finite-type k-scheme W with a closed point w and smooth morphisms W -> Hilb^d(A^3_k) and W -> C sending w to [Γ] and v, respectively?
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper's Problem XXVII in §2.6, not at a theorem or conjecture from another section. The wording there is essentially the same open problem: a point [Γ] on the smoothable component of Hilb^d(A^3) with tangent space dimension 3d+6, and the question whether its local singularity is smoothly equivalent to the cone point over Gr(2,6). To make the question fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper, I only unpacked notation and hidden conventions supplied elsewhere in the paper: the global convention that the base field is algebraically closed (§1.3), the definition of the smoothable component (§2.1), and the exact meaning of smooth equivalence together with its geometric reformulation (§2.6). I did not add any characteristic-zero, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency restrictions, because this open problem is not stated with such hypotheses in the paper.
